tasks.title: Fix 2 flaky folder_sync timing tests (CI fails at random)
tasks.desc:
CI now fails at random: since TD-01 started running pdf_android tests in CI, two pre-existing folder_sync tests fail on slow runners (CI runs 204 and 206; the same commits pass on rerun):
- `annotation_worker_serializes_snapshots_to_sqlite_before_export_delay`: requires a background SQLite save within 600 ms
- `failed_export_does_not_block_local_sqlite_save_for_another_pdf`
Neither was changed today; they rely on wall-clock time.
Done means: both tests still prove what they prove now (save happens before the export delay; a failed export doesn't block other saves), but without timing bounds a slow machine can break, and the pdf_android suite passes repeatedly under heavy load.

notes.text: Added CI evidence: 2 failing tests, runs 204 and 206

Now failing in most CI runs (210, 211, 212). Worth checking while fixing: whether the worker's export path got slower (e.g. CO-01's fsync in export_markdown_to_file), since both tests assert the local save does not wait behind export.
Approved in chat ("yeah go further in the plan"). (relayed from chat by the agent)

Plan: an agent rewrites the 2 folder_sync timing tests test-first (first prove the flake reproducibly under load, then remove the wall-clock dependency while keeping what they check); also check whether CO-01's fsync slowed the export path. Orchestrator reviews and merges.

The two folder_sync tests that made CI fail at random now check the order of events instead of elapsed time, so a slow machine can't break them.
- Root cause: the code never waited on the export debounce or backoff. The 600 ms / 1 s limits were really measuring how fast the machine saves (each save does 2 fsynced journal writes + SQLite).
- TDD verified by the orchestrator: a test-only "slow machine" switch (1.5 s per save) makes both old tests fail every time (2 failures); after the rewrite they pass with it on. Debounce/backoff are set to 1 hour in these tests, so a save that waited on them would time out. The agent broke the code on purpose both ways and each test caught it.
- 30 loaded runs (8 parallel, CPUs saturated): 30/30 pass. Production timings unchanged (700 ms debounce, 5 s retry).
- Finding, not changed (your design call): exports and local saves share one worker thread. A save that arrives during a running export waits for that one export to finish, which can be noticeable for a large PDF.
- Not related: CO-01's fsync change is not on this path (only the desktop app uses that export).
- Possible follow-up: another nearby test compares two clock readings (`> 4 s`); not seen flaky.
Accepted in chat: excellent review. Tablet checklists to be run later; reopen if anything is wrong. (relayed from chat by the agent)
